title: 6.27.4 Lab: Set up the board
description: Fill the empty grid: black on the dark squares of the top three rows, red on the bottom three. The drawing is already there, so the board appears as the letters do.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The board is drawn, but there are no pieces, and the top says `Checkers: 0 red, 0 black`. `makeBoard` builds 8 rows of 8 cells and every cell is `''`, so there is nothing to draw.

steps.title: Black on the top rows
steps.instructions: In `makeBoard`, on the line before `row.push(p)`, put a black piece on every dark square of rows 0, 1 and 2: `if ((r + c) % 2 === 1 && r < 3) p = 'b';`. Run: twelve black pieces, and the top says `0 red, 12 black`.
hints: `(r + c) % 2 === 1` is a dark square; `r < 3` is rows 0, 1 and 2.
The line goes before `row.push(p)`: once `p` is pushed, changing it changes nothing in the row.

steps.title: Red on the bottom rows
steps.instructions: Below it, the same for red on rows 5, 6 and 7: `if ((r + c) % 2 === 1 && r > 4) p = 'r';`. Run: `12 red, 12 black`, with two empty rows in the middle.
hints: `r > 4` is true on rows 5, 6 and 7. `r >= 5` says the same.
Count the pieces in one row: 4. Three rows of 4 is 12.

steps.title: Read the grid
steps.instructions: Nothing to type here. In `drawPieces`, find where a cell's letter picks the circle's colour, and in `countPieces`, how the count is made. Change `r < 3` to `r < 2` and Run: black has 8 pieces, and the count follows the grid. Put it back to `r < 3`.

requirements.title: A dark-square test with % 2
requirements.description: A piece is placed only on a dark square, tested with % 2 on the row plus the column. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)

requirements.title: Black on the top rows
requirements.description: Black pieces ('b') go on the top three rows, rows 0, 1 and 2. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)

requirements.title: Red on the bottom rows
requirements.description: Red pieces ('r') go on the bottom three rows, rows 5, 6 and 7. Help: 6.27.2 (Reading: A board is a grid of letters)
